title: Flat covering pullbacks jointly reflect module isomorphisms
statement: Let $X$ and $Y_i$ ($i\in I$) be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $f_i:Y_i\to X$ be flat morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism] such that for every $x\in X$ some $y\in Y_i$ satisfies $f_i(y)=x$. Let $\varphi:P\to Q$ be a morphism of arbitrary sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If every pullback $f_i^*\varphi$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is an isomorphism, then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use joint surjectivity to choose, for each x, an i and y over x. The scheme stalk map O_X,x to O_Y_i,y is local and flat, hence faithfully flat. This is the Flat.stalkMap and Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom argument in the existing source proof.

For any O_Y_i,y-module J, the skyscraper module at y represents linear maps from a stalk to J. Precomposition with f_i^*phi is bijective because this map is invertible. The pullback/pushforward adjunction transfers this bijectivity to maps into the pushed-forward skyscraper; the explicit pushforwardSkyscraperIso identifies it with a skyscraper at x. Therefore precomposition with phi_x is bijective on linear maps to every O_Y_i,y-module J. The source lemma LinearMap.bijective_of_bijective_comp uses tensor-Hom adjunction and Yoneda to show that scalar extension of phi_x is bijective, and faithfully flat descent of bijectivity shows that phi_x is bijective. All these arguments are already proved, without sorry, in the cited source module.
Every stalk map of phi is bijective. Apply the stalk criterion for module isomorphisms, implemented by the source lemma isIso_of_bijective_stalkLinearMap, to conclude that phi is invertible.
